notes.text: Quinn Hughes is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 52% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 67:11 together, about what it had with Hughes (56%).

Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 48% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 90:20 together, about what it had with Määttä (48%).
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, down from 34% last season.
Danila Yurov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 28 games, up from 6% last season.
Erik Gustafsson is out 2-4 weeks and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Brian Dumoulin has taken his spot beside Brandt Clarke.

stakes: The Wild go in first in the NHL with 42 points, the Kings seventh in the Pacific with 20 points.

LAK.head: Leaning the Kings’ way
LAK.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Los Angeles has home-ice advantage, while Minnesota will be without Hughes. Still, it’s close: the Wild can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: Fiala’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kings have won two in a row, while the Wild (18-4-6) lost 4-3 in a shootout to Colorado on Friday. Going in, the Wild are first in the NHL and the Kings seventh in the Pacific (29th in the NHL).

The Wild’s record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.633), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Kings have played better than their record (.435) says: their chances are worth about .593, and their finishing has held them back. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.
This season, the Kings have been outscored 74-64, but only 41-38 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 22-17.

The Wild block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and draw more penalties than they take (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.29 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. As for the Kings, they leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest) and keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st), but take a lot of low-quality shots (28th). The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Kings. On top of that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Kirill Kaprizov (19 G / 30 A / 49 P in 28 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is second in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Minnesota. Adrian Kempe (7 G / 8 A / 15 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind.

Jesper Wallstedt (16-3-5 / .918 SV% in 24 GS) has been outstanding for Minnesota and will likely start. Los Angeles has two options in net: Darcy Kuemper (9-5-1 / .891 SV% in 15 GS) and Anton Forsberg (0-7-1 / .901 SV% in 8 GS). Kuemper has started seven of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday, so Los Angeles could turn to Forsberg to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
